title: Enterprise usage export: intake gating, SLA-driven prioritization, and templated outputs
creator: Avery Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Large enterprise customers submit ad-hoc requests for granular usage exports, cost breakdowns, and tenant-level dashboards. Intake is ad-hoc, engineering triage lacks context, and high-effort exports slip SLAs or duplicate work. We need a repeatable intake + prioritization playbook that: 1) captures required context up-front, 2) gates requests by SLA tier and engineering effort, 3) offers templated export formats and self-serve options for common cases, and 4) routes work to Dedicated/Private support paths when sensitive data or export retention policies are required.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-response for enterprise export requests to 24 business hours for P1/P0 customers.
- Decrease bespoke export engineering effort by 40% through templates and self-serve bundles.
- Ensure security/compliance gate is applied consistently for exports touching customer PII or cross-tenant joins.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Design an intake form and triage rubric tied to SLA/contract tier and engineering estimated effort.
- Define a set of 6 standard export templates (usage-by-workspace, cost-by-route, token-class-breakdown, rate-limited historical window, per-API-key aggregation, and tenant-linked cost-allocation) and sample CSV/Parquet schemas.
- Create routing rules: self-serve, PM approval, engineering backlog, or security-led review.
- Document runbook for Delivery team on one-off exports and required audit logs.

Out of scope:
- Building the full export job scheduler (will be a follow-up ENG epc).
- Billing system-level contract enforcement (coordination item with Finance).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype available in Confluence and connected to a tracking tag for priority calculation
Triage rubric documented with examples and automated score mapping to routing buckets
Six export template schemas (CSV and Parquet) uploaded to shared Drive with sample queries
Routing rules coded as Issue triage playbook (manual steps documented) and handed to Solutions Engineering
Security checklist created and sign-off process defined for exports involving PII
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers completed and time-to-first-response metric measured
comments: 2026-02-28 - Avery Patel: Created initial ticket after intake workshop with AE and Solutions Engineering. Collected 12 sample customer requests from support triage. Marked customer_impact as high due to SLA complaints.

2026-03-02 - Sofia Ramos: Scoping meeting notes: prioritize reusable templates first. Engineering flagged costs for historical joins and recommended limiting default retention windows to 90 days (opt-in to longer).
2026-03-04 - Rajiv Menon (Eng): ENG asks for concrete sample data and estimated CPU hours for 30-day export. Requested that templates include pre-aggregated buckets to avoid expensive JOINs.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Maya Chen): Proposed intake form mockups with conditional fields based on data sensitivity. Suggested a checkbox to surface PII concerns that triggers Security review.

2026-03-08 - PM decision: Move forward with 6 templates + intake form MVP. Trade-off: accept narrower default retention to reduce compute costs; long-tail requests will require engineering ticket and higher SLA tier.
2026-03-10 - Security (Lena Fischer): Preliminary security checklist drafted. Need to confirm KMS/HSM usage requirements and audit-log retention for exports >30 days.
2026-03-12 - Sofia Ramos: Draft Confluence intake form and triage rubric uploaded (link below). Ready for pilot outreach to three customers (Acct 72, Acct 108, Acct 215).
